title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page continues Grothendieck's group-theoretic bookkeeping in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. That is the sequel to the 1981 'Longue Marche'. Its theme is profinite fundamental groups and braid/Teichmüller-type groups, and the loop relations satisfied by inertia/loop generators, as in the Galois action on pi_1 of the projective line minus three points.

Objects. Two 'points' or loop classes are labelled rho and sigma. Attached to them are:
- normalizers N_rho, N_sigma;
- centralizers Z_rho, Z_sigma and 'special' centralizers SZ_rho = L_rho, SZ_sigma = L_sigma (the loop subgroups, procyclic-like);
- a group G^+_{rho,sigma}, with special subgroup G_{rho,sigma} = SG_{rho,sigma};
- a central subgroup mu (roots of unity, or a centre of order 2), with copies mu_rho, mu_sigma.
On the previous page M_{rho,sigma} is a fibre product of these normalizers over a quotient gamma_{rho,sigma}. A subgroup M^⇆_{rho,sigma} ⊂ M_{rho,sigma} is singled out, and an exact sequence 1 -> mu_rho -> M^⇆ -> G_{rho,sigma} -> 1 is identified with the given group M.

This page:
- (56) gives the canonical maps M ≅ M^⇆_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho ↪ M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho. This realizes the global group M inside the 'local' group attached to the pair (rho, sigma), modulo the central mu_rho.
- A marginal definition sets Gamma^⇆ := M^⇆/G^+ ⊂ Gamma := M_{rho,sigma}/G^+.
- (57) is a morphism of extensions. The top row is 1 -> mu_rho × G_{rho,sigma} -> M^⇆ -> gamma_{rho,sigma} -> 1. The bottom row is 1 -> SZ_rho × SZ_sigma × G^+ -> M_{rho,sigma} -> Gamma_{rho,sigma} -> 1.
- Under (56), the subgroup G^{+∧} of M corresponds to (mu_rho × G^+)/mu_sigma ≅ G_{rho,sigma}. It maps isomorphically onto G_{rho,sigma} ⊂ M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho.
- (58) is a three-row ladder of extensions:
  - 1 -> G^{+∧} (≅ G^+) -> M -> Pi~_Q (≅ gamma_{rho,sigma}) -> 1;
  - 1 -> G^+ -> M^⇆/mu_rho -> Gamma^⇆/mu_rho -> 1;
  - 1 -> G^+ -> M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho -> Gamma_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho -> 1.
  The vertical maps are an isomorphism followed by inclusions.
- Conclusion (59). The canonical epimorphism 1 -> L_rho × L_sigma -> Gamma_{rho,sigma} -> gamma_{rho,sigma} -> 1 admits a 'bisection' given by Gamma^⇆, whose intersection with SZ_rho × SZ_sigma is mu_rho × 1. Equivalently, after dividing by mu_rho, the extension splits: Gamma/mu_rho is the semidirect product of a copy of gamma ≅ Pi~_Q with (L_rho/mu_rho) × L_sigma. This is made explicit as formula (56) on the next page.

Purpose. The aim is to express the quotient group Pi~_Q (a Teichmüller/Galois-type quotient attached to Q) as a section of the 'two-loop' group Gamma_{rho,sigma}. The next page then transports the special subgroups M(0), M[0], etc. through this identification, which requires defining analogues in general M_{rho,sigma}.

Overall, the page is routine diagram chasing with extensions and central quotients.
errors: Internal inconsistency: the page writes gamma_{rho,sigma} ≅ Gamma^⇆_{rho,sigma} while also stating that Gamma^⇆ meets SZ_rho × SZ_sigma in mu_rho × 1. Since Gamma^⇆ surjects onto gamma, it is Gamma^⇆/mu_rho that is isomorphic to gamma, as the next page correctly writes. The 'bisection' is a genuine section only modulo mu_rho.

In (57) the right-hand vertical is drawn as '‖' between gamma_{rho,sigma} and Gamma_{rho,sigma}. Since the kernels differ by L_rho × L_sigma versus mu_rho, this should be an inclusion Gamma^⇆ ⊂ Gamma, not an equality. The symbol appears to be overwritten.
Equation numbering is unstable: (55) is used twice on the previous page, and (56) is reused on the next page.

The identifications G_{rho,sigma} = SG_{rho,sigma} ≅ G^{+∧} and '(mu_rho × G^+)/mu_sigma ≅ G_{rho,sigma}' are stated loosely. The role of the quotient by mu_sigma versus mu_rho is not fully explained on this page.

ideas.what: Realizing a global group M as a central quotient of a subgroup M^⇆ of a fibre product of normalizers of two loop subgroups: M ≅ M^⇆/mu_rho ⊂ M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho
ideas.modern_name: fibre products of normalizers of inertia/cusp subgroups; central extensions; local-global description of (profinite) mapping class / braid groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; in the anabelian/Teichmüller context, work around GT (Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak)
ideas.where_published: Theme related to La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme; this specific construction unknown

ideas.what: Splitting ('bisection') of the extension 1 -> L_rho × L_sigma -> Gamma_{rho,sigma} -> gamma_{rho,sigma} -> 1 modulo the central mu_rho, giving a semidirect product decomposition Gamma/mu_rho ≅ gamma ⋉ (L_rho/mu_rho × L_sigma)
ideas.modern_name: split extension / semidirect product decomposition of normalizer quotients of cusp subgroups

deep.surprise_reason: The page is technical diagram chasing with central extensions, setting up notation for identifying subgroups in the next pages. There is no new conceptual idea or finished result here that a specialist would find absent from the literature, beyond the general fact that this whole 'équation des lacets' manuscript is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note (written diagonally at the top left): 'On prend donc Γ^⇆_{ρ,σ} déf= M^⇆_{ρ,σ}/G^+_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Γ_{ρ,σ} = M_{ρ,σ}/G^+_{ρ,σ}'. The reading is correct, but it is a marginal addition, not part of the main text.
In (57), top row: the superscript on G_{ρ,σ} is struck out. The intended term is likely μ_ρ × G_{ρ,σ}, and the struck mark looks like '+' rather than '±'.
In (57), right column: the vertical sign between γ_{ρ,σ} and Γ_{ρ,σ} is drawn over a corrected letter. The bottom entry Γ_{ρ,σ} is written over an earlier symbol.
In (58), the top row's left vertical arrow is a double/iso arrow; the first map in the middle row looks like '⇒' (an iso-marked arrow); the middle vertical arrow is labelled 2 (or z).

In (59), the struck text before 'Γ^⇆_{ρ,σ}' reads approximately 'Π^⇆_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ', with 'γ_{ρ,σ} ≅' written above it. The final parenthesis reads '(dont l'intersection avec [-L_ρ-] SZ_ρ × SZ_σ est μ_ρ × 1)'.
'Ainsi, on trouve un prolongement que l'homomorphisme' should probably read 'Ainsi, on trouve en passant que l'homomorphisme canonique épi ...'.
